"""Ports: interfaces the storage layer must satisfy. Do not change this file."""
from typing import Protocol, Any


class Repository(Protocol):
    def insert(self, obj: Any) -> int: ...          # stores obj, assigns and returns a new id (ids start at 1)
    def fetch(self, obj_id: int) -> Any | None: ...  # None if missing OR soft-deleted
    def fetch_all(self) -> list: ...                 # live (not deleted) objects, ascending id
    def mark_deleted(self, obj_id: int) -> bool: ... # soft delete; False if missing or already deleted

arguments.why: Create the audit log module for tracking create/delete operations

task:
Task: Implement these features in the package:
1. Pagination: api.page(cursor=None, size=2) returns {"items": [...], "next": cursor_or_None} over live books in ascending id; `cursor` is the id after which to continue (live ids greater than cursor, even if the cursor item was deleted since); `next` is the id of the last item returned when more live items remain, and None otherwise, even if the last page is exactly full.
2. Audit log: every successful create and delete appends an event dict {"op": "create"|"delete", "id": n} to a log kept in a NEW module app/audit.py. api.history() returns {"events": [...]} in order; failed operations are not logged. api.reset() must also clear the log.
3. Soft delete: api.delete(item_id) marks the Book deleted (returns {"ok": True}, or {"error": "not_found"} if missing or already deleted). Deleted books must disappear from get, list_all and page, but their ids are never reused (the audit history keeps its events).
4. Make the storage class in app/store.py implement the Repository protocol in app/ports.py exactly (method names and behaviour as documented there), and update every caller to use those methods. Keep all existing api behaviour.
Keep the existing tests passing.
